content:
Last Friday (21st), the verdict in the Hong Kong Alliance case was delivered at the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. In the early hours, a woman who was queuing for a public hearing was taken away by police officers in a police van. In response to enquiries, the police stated that the woman was arrested on three charges, including "behaving in a disorderly manner in a public place", "resisting or wilfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of his duty", and "with seditious intent".

Around 5 a.m. last Friday, more than fifty people were already queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. During the process, a plainclothes police officer pointed out that a woman in the queue was "suspected of wearing clothing printed with seditious words", and subsequently took her into a police van. While officers were taking the woman away, several officers repeatedly directed reporters to leave, saying "take you to the press area", and immediately erected an orange-red cordon extending to Nga Wah Street. After the woman boarded the police van, they immediately dismantled the cordon. On that day, a "courtwatch companion" who was queuing near the woman said that she was wearing a black T-shirt printed with Japanese text.

集誌社 (The Collective) made enquiries to the police regarding the reasons for taking away the woman, and whether an arrest had been made. The police replied this morning (24th) that during a security operation near the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts on 21 August, a 45-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of "behaving in a disorderly manner in a public place", "resisting or wilfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of his duty", and "with seditious intent", and was detained for investigation.
